object_sets.description: Every object that the bundle holds: each DCMP-2 message and EBMP-2 event in envelopes and each record in observations.

Each signing key of each object of the bundle, carried proofs and approval records among them, and each signing key of each time attestation that a trusted-time countersignature of those objects carries.

Each signing key of each envelope and observation payload, whether or not its signature counts. Excludes signatures on time attestations. Report indexes identify the containing envelope or observation.
Each signing key of each time attestation, whether or not its signature counts. Report indexes identify the envelope or observation carrying the countersignature.

Each signature entry of each object in envelopes and observations, with the trusted-time countersignatures that cover it and the signature entries of their attestations. An object without a countersignature is in the set, so that the item is not established while any object has a signature that no countersignature covers.
Each decision response that the bundle holds.
Each decision request of the bundle with the response and the events that EBMP2-058 pairs with it, and each continuation with the objects that it names (EBMP2-078).
Each execution_released event with the request, the response and the terminal events of its attempt.
Each entry of ecl.ext.obligation-discharge.v1 on an execution_released event, with the proof that it names.
Each side effect of a succeeded terminal event.

checks.description: Each envelope satisfies its schema and the verifier's limits, its payload is canonical and matches its digest and media type, and its payload-bound policy is usable (INTEGRITY-ENVELOPE-1 IE1-040 steps 1 to 5; EBMP2-068 stage 2).
No object's own time and no attested time is later than the evaluation time.

Each object-signing dependency is valid at its own evaluation time under the payload's policy, including accepted suites, eligible keys, purpose, principal, validity and signature verification; the signatures that count meet the threshold. Time-attestation dependencies are checked by attestation-signers.

The caller's current policy has no revocation of an object-signing dependency's key identifier or public key effective at or before that dependency's own time. Time-attestation dependencies are covered by attestation-signers.
Each trusted-time countersignature is valid and binds the payload and the signatures that it covers.
Every signature of every object is covered by a valid trusted-time countersignature.

Every time-attestation signing dependency, including an uncounted signature, meets IE1-040 step 6 at the attested time under the attestation payload's accepted suites and eligible keys, and the named and current policies' effective revocations. This is stronger than threshold validity of the attestation.
Each trust dependency's key is held by the caller's current policy with the public key that the historical check used, unrevoked and within its validity interval at the evaluation time.
Each signed object satisfies its schema.
Each signed object satisfies its semantic rules.
Each observation is an EBMP-2 verification event.
No two objects of the bundle, in envelopes and observations together, have one identifier.
Each decision response records its decision basis.
No input recorded as verifiable has the request's actor as its source.

Each decision basis names the supplied register version and matches its declared inputs, classes, required flags, sources and derivations. Recorded input timing is compared with declared deadlines and maximum ages only when the necessary fields are supplied (DCMP2-053). This check does not re-evaluate policy or approval thresholds.

The recorded timestamps needed for every applicable available-input maximum-age or acquisition-deadline comparison are supplied. Bounds are checked by decision-basis-register; recorded times are not established as true.
Objects pair by identity: one request per identity and attempt, one response per request, a unique response for each authority event and a request for each event.

Each continuation names the request, challenge response and approval that DCMP2-056 requires and relates to the continued request as it requires; lists the response and the approval among its causal predecessors by identifier and digest; and no challenge has two admitted continuations (denied or challenged continuations do not violate this uniqueness condition); and, when the continuation's response is an admit, rests on an approval whose signing keys hold ecl.purpose.approval.v1, none of them bound to the request's actor, and whose required expires_at is later than the evaluated_at of that response.
Each response binds its request.
Each event binds its request, response and authority, with the digests and use counts that they name.
Each recorded release lies within the authorization's window with the release guard, and no terminal records a release that may have come after valid_until.
Every causal predecessor of every object is an object of the bundle.
Every causal predecessor reference carries the predecessor's recomputed canonical digest.
The causal graph over every object is acyclic.

Every held predecessor has its successor's root trace and is in the same workflow with an attempt no greater, its declared parent workflow, or a child workflow. A child-to-parent join requires a digest-bound path through that child's ancestry to its creating or delegating parent object; an absent origin leaves the relationship unresolved.
Within one workflow, every predecessor has a lower sequence than its successor.
The states of each execution attempt move only forward.
Every request has a terminal event.

Each attempt with running execution, or with terminal state succeeded, failed, partially_succeeded, unknown, rolled_back or compensated, has its authority_consumed and release events, and each released attempt under a single-use authorization has its authority_consumed event. The check runs whatever the closure of the rest of the bundle and is silent only for an attempt whose own objects name a predecessor that the bundle does not hold.

Each release records a discharge of every required pre-release obligation; the entry, result, binding, time and carried-proof digest satisfy EBMP2-070 conditions 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6, under the specified gates and precedence.

Each carried ECL proof satisfies the issuer and purpose, admitted type and exchange binding, and freshness checks of EBMP2-070 conditions 5, 7 and 8, including its stated issuer/purpose exception; an uncarried proof or unnamed issuer does not establish proof scope.
Each terminal event carries the outcome reason that EBMP2-056 requires, and no other.

The terminal state is succeeded and it lists at least one side effect. For each listed side effect, a historically valid verification observation names the terminal event by identifier and digest, has its workflow, trace and attempt, the side effect's subject and digest, decision pass, a time no earlier, another principal and disjoint keys.

trust_knowledge.description: The version of the caller's trust policy that an object or an attestation names, among the versions the caller supplies (TP1-001).
The caller's current trust policy at the evaluation time.
The revocations of the caller's current trust policy, applied at each trust dependency's own time (TP1-006).
The Consequential Action Register that the caller supplies (DCMP2-053).
No trust input: the check reads the bundle's objects only.

waivers.description: The caller's explicit acceptance of current trust failures for one run: the verdict is verified instead of current-trust-failed and the report states the acceptance. It changes the verdict only: an item whose failure it accepts, current-trust, stays not established, no item is established over less than its whole object set, and an invalid or incomplete verdict never changes.

items.condition: When the caller supplied a register.
When a register is supplied and at least one recorded available input has a declared maximum age or acquisition deadline.
When the verifier applied EBMP2-070 to an execution_released event whose response carries an obligation to be met before release.
When the response that an execution_released event records carries an obligation to be met during or after execution.
